4	constant-bias, left-endpoint kinematic propagation and, at IMU timestamps
5	carrying an external pose observation, right-composes a gain-scaled SE(3)
6	correction onto the predicted pose. The result is one immutable
7	:class:`FusionState` per IMU sample.
8	
9	Conventions follow :mod:`mappilot.geometry` and :mod:`mappilot.inertial`
10	(right-handed coordinates; a pose maps body coordinates to world
11	coordinates):
12	
13	* Each IMU sample is ``(timestamp, acceleration, angular_velocity)`` with
14	  the same record semantics as :func:`mappilot.inertial.preintegrate_imu`.
15	  At least two samples with strictly increasing timestamps are required.
16	* Each pose observation is ``(timestamp, pose)`` where ``pose`` is the
17	  observed body-to-world :class:`~mappilot.geometry.Pose3`. Observation
18	  timestamps must be strictly increasing, may be empty, and every
19	  timestamp must equal an IMU timestamp exactly; duplicate observations at
20	  one instant are forbidden.
21	* Between adjacent IMU times ``t[k]`` and ``t[k+1]`` the bias-corrected
22	  measurement of the *left* sample ``k`` is held constant. The pose
23	  propagates as
24	
25	  ``R_new = R * Exp((omega - b_g) * dt)``
26	
27	  and the corrected specific force is rotated with the rotation ``R`` at
28	  the beginning of the interval:
29	
30	  ``a_world = R * (a - b_a) + gravity``
31	  ``p_new = p + v * dt + 0.5 * a_world * dt**2``
32	  ``v_new = v + a_world * dt``
33	
34	* At an observation time the residual is
35	  ``error = T_pred.inverse().compose(T_obs)``. Its translation norm and the
36	  norm of the rotation part of ``Pose3.log(error)`` (its first three
37	  components) are tested against ``residual_threshold``; when a threshold
38	  is given, either norm strictly exceeding it rejects the observation
39	  (equality is accepted), leaving the predicted state untouched.
40	* An accepted observation scales the rotation and translation parts of
41	  ``Pose3.log(error)`` with ``rotation_gain`` and ``translation_gain``
42	  respectively; the ``Pose3.exp`` of the scaled tangent vector is
43	  right-composed onto the predicted pose. Velocity is never changed by an
44	  observation. An observation at the first IMU time corrects the initial
45	  state in exactly the same way.
46	
47	This module is pure Python and depends only on the standard library plus
48	:mod:`mappilot.geometry`. Importing it never starts the HTTP service.
49	
50	Validation policy mirrors :mod:`mappilot.inertial`: non-iterable samples or
51	records, malformed records, wrong vector dimensions, non-real scalars
52	(including booleans), a pose of the wrong type, or a threshold/gain of the
53	wrong type raise :class:`TypeError`; fewer than two IMU samples,
54	non-finite values, timestamps that are not strictly increasing in either
55	sequence, an observation timestamp that does not hit an IMU sample, a gain
56	outside ``[0, 1]``, a negative or non-finite threshold, and non-finite
57	propagation results raise :class:`ValueError`.
58	"""
59	
60	from __future__ import annotations
61	
62	import math
63	import numbers
64	from typing import Iterable, NamedTuple
65	
66	from .geometry import Pose3
67	
68	__all__ = ["FusionState", "fuse_imu_pose"]
69	
70	_ZERO_VECTOR = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
71

73	class FusionState(NamedTuple):
74	    """Filter state at one IMU timestamp.
75	
76	    Immutable. ``pose`` is the body-to-world :class:`~mappilot.geometry.Pose3`
77	    and ``velocity`` is the world-frame velocity after applying any
78	    observation at this timestamp. ``observation_used`` is ``None`` when no
79	    observation exists at this timestamp, ``True`` when one was applied,
80	    and ``False`` when one was present but rejected by the residual gate.
81	    """
82	
83	    timestamp: float
84	    pose: Pose3
85	    velocity: tuple[float, float, float]
86	    observation_used: bool | None
87	
88	
89	def _real_scalar(value: object, name: str) -> float:
90	    """Coerce one real, non-boolean scalar to float (finiteness checked by caller)."""
91	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, numbers.Real):
92	        raise TypeError(f"{name} must be a real number, got {type(value).__name__}")
93	    return float(value)
94	
95	
96	def _finite_scalar(value: object, name: str) -> float:
97	    """Coerce one real, finite, non-boolean scalar to float."""
98	    result = _real_scalar(value, name)
99	    if not math.isfinite(result):
100	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be finite, got {result!r}")
101	    return result
102	
103	
104	def _vector3(value: object, name: str) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
105	    """Validate one vector of exactly three finite, non-boolean real scalars."""
106	    if isinstance(value, (str, bytes, bytearray)):
107	        raise TypeError(f"{name} must be a sequence of 3 real numbers")
108	    try:
109	        items = tuple(value)  # type: ignore[call-overload]
110	    except TypeError:
111	        raise TypeError(f"{name} must be a sequence of 3 real numbers") from None
112	    if len(items) != 3:
113	        raise TypeError(f"{name} must have 3 elements, got {len(items)}")
114	    return (
115	        _finite_scalar(items[0], f"{name}[0]"),
116	        _finite_scalar(items[1], f"{name}[1]"),
117	        _finite_scalar(items[2], f"{name}[2]"),
118	    )
119	
120	
121	def _unpack_sample(
122	    sample: object, index: int
123	) -> tuple[float, tuple[float, float, float], tuple[float, float, float]]:
124	    """Validate one ``(timestamp, acceleration, angular_velocity)`` sample."""
125	    if isinstance(sample, (str, bytes, bytearray)):
126	        raise TypeError(
127	            f"imu_samples[{index}] must be a (timestamp, acceleration, "
128	            "angular_velocity) triple"
129	        )
130	    try:
131	        items = tuple(sample)  # type: ignore[call-overload]
132	    except TypeError:
133	        raise TypeError(
134	            f"imu_samples[{index}] must be a (timestamp, acceleration, "
135	            "angular_velocity) triple"
136	        ) from None
137	    if len(items) != 3:
138	        raise TypeError(
139	            f"imu_samples[{index}] must have exactly 3 elements "
140	            f"(timestamp, acceleration, angular_velocity), got {len(items)}"
141	        )
142	    timestamp = _finite_scalar(items[0], f"imu_samples[{index}][0]")
143	    acceleration = _vector3(items[1], f"imu_samples[{index}][1]")
144	    angular_velocity = _vector3(items[2], f"imu_samples[{index}][2]")
145	    return timestamp, acceleration, angular_velocity
146	
147	
148	def _unpack_observation(
149	    observation: object, index: int
150	) -> tuple[float, Pose3]:
151	    """Validate one ``(timestamp, pose)`` observation."""
152	    if isinstance(observation, (str, bytes, bytearray)):
153	        raise TypeError(
154	            f"pose_observations[{index}] must be a (timestamp, pose) pair"
155	        )
156	    try:
157	        items = tuple(observation)  # type: ignore[call-overload]
158	    except TypeError:
159	        raise TypeError(
160	            f"pose_observations[{index}] must be a (timestamp, pose) pair"
161	        ) from None
162	    if len(items) != 2:
163	        raise TypeError(
164	            f"pose_observations[{index}] must have exactly 2 elements "
165	            f"(timestamp, pose), got {len(items)}"
166	        )
167	    timestamp = _finite_scalar(items[0], f"pose_observations[{index}][0]")
168	    pose = items[1]
169	    if not isinstance(pose, Pose3):
170	        raise TypeError(
171	            f"pose_observations[{index}][1] must be a Pose3, got "
172	            f"{type(pose).__name__}"
173	        )
174	    return timestamp, pose
175	
176	
177	def _gain(value: object, name: str) -> float:
178	    """Validate one correction gain: a finite real in [0, 1]."""
179	    result = _real_scalar(value, name)
180	    if not math.isfinite(result):
181	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be finite, got {result!r}")
182	    if not 0.0 <= result <= 1.0:
183	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must lie in [0, 1], got {result!r}")
184	    return result
185	
186	
187	def _threshold(value: object) -> float | None:
188	    """Validate an optional residual gate: ``None`` or a finite non-negative real."""
189	    if value is None:
190	        return None
191	    result = _real_scalar(value, "residual_threshold")
192	    if not math.isfinite(result):
193	        raise ValueError(f"residual_threshold must be finite, got {result!r}")
194	    if result < 0.0:
195	        raise ValueError(
196	            f"residual_threshold must be non-negative, got {result!r}"
197	        )
198	    return result
199	
200	
201	def _finite_state(
202	    translation: tuple[float, float, float],
203	    quaternion: tuple[float, float, float, float],
204	    velocity: tuple[float, float, float],
205	) -> None:
206	    for component in (*translation, *quaternion, *velocity):
207	        if not math.isfinite(component):
208	            raise ValueError("IMU propagation produced non-finite state")
209	
210	
211	def fuse_imu_pose(
212	    imu_samples: Iterable[
213	        tuple[float, tuple[float, float, float], tuple[float, float, float]]
214	    ],
215	    pose_observations: Iterable[tuple[float, Pose3]],
216	    initial_pose: Pose3,
217	    initial_velocity: Iterable[float],
218	    accelerometer_bias: Iterable[float] = _ZERO_VECTOR,
219	    gyroscope_bias: Iterable[float] = _ZERO_VECTOR,
220	    gravity: Iterable[float] = _ZERO_VECTOR,
221	    translation_gain: float = 1.0,
222	    rotation_gain: float = 1.0,
223	    residual_threshold: float | None = None,
224	) -> tuple[FusionState, ...]:
225	    """Fuse strapdown IMU propagation with timestamped pose observations.
226	
227	    Parameters
228	    ----------
229	    imu_samples:
230	        ``(timestamp, acceleration, angular_velocity)`` records with
231	        strictly increasing absolute timestamps (seconds); at least two
232	        samples. The iterable is consumed exactly once.
233	    pose_observations:
234	        ``(timestamp, pose)`` pairs ordered by strictly increasing
235	        timestamps; the sequence may be empty. Each timestamp must equal an
236	        IMU timestamp exactly and no timestamp may repeat. The iterable is
237	        consumed exactly once.
238	    initial_pose:
239	        Body-to-world :class:`~mappilot.geometry.Pose3` at the first IMU
240	        timestamp.
241	    initial_velocity:
242	        World-frame velocity 3-vector at the first IMU timestamp.
243	    accelerometer_bias, gyroscope_bias:
244	        Constant body-frame 3-vector biases subtracted from the
245	        acceleration and angular-rate measurements; zero by default.
246	    gravity:
247	        World-frame gravity 3-vector added to the rotated specific force;
248	        zero by default.
249	    translation_gain, rotation_gain:
250	        Gains in ``[0, 1]`` scaling the translation and rotation parts of
251	        each applied correction; 1.0 by default (full correction).
252	    residual_threshold:
253	        ``None`` (default, no gating) or a non-negative finite bound; an
254	        observation is rejected when the residual translation norm or
255	        rotation norm is strictly greater than it. Equality is accepted.
256	
257	    Returns
258	    -------
259	    tuple[FusionState, ...]
260	        One immutable :class:`FusionState` per IMU sample, in timestamp
261	        order, each carrying the pose (and world velocity) after any
262	        observation at that timestamp. ``observation_used`` is ``None``
263	        without an observation, ``True`` when one was applied, and
264	        ``False`` when the gate rejected one.
265	
266	    Raises
267	    ------
268	    TypeError
269	        Non-iterable inputs or records, malformed records, wrong vector
270	        dimensions, non-real or boolean values, an ``initial_pose`` or
271	        observed pose that is not a :class:`~mappilot.geometry.Pose3`, or
272	        gains/threshold of the wrong numeric type.
273	    ValueError
274	        Fewer than two IMU samples; non-finite values; timestamps that are
275	        not strictly increasing in either sequence; an observation
276	        timestamp missing from the IMU timeline; a gain outside ``[0, 1]``;
277	        a negative or non-finite threshold; or non-finite propagation
278	        results.
279	    """
280	    if not isinstance(initial_pose, Pose3):
281	        raise TypeError(
282	            f"initial_pose must be a Pose3, got {type(initial_pose).__name__}"
283	        )
284	    velocity0 = _vector3(initial_velocity, "initial_velocity")
285	    accel_bias = _vector3(accelerometer_bias, "accelerometer_bias")
286	    gyro_bias = _vector3(gyroscope_bias, "gyroscope_bias")
287	    gravity_vector = _vector3(gravity, "gravity")
288	    t_gain = _gain(translation_gain, "translation_gain")
289	    r_gain = _gain(rotation_gain, "rotation_gain")
290	    threshold = _threshold(residual_threshold)
291	
292	    # Materialize both iterables exactly once; validated records are freshly
293	    # built floats and Pose3 values are immutable, so caller objects are
294	    # never mutated or aliased into mutable state.
295	    if isinstance(imu_samples, (str, bytes, bytearray)):
296	        raise TypeError(
297	            "imu_samples must be an iterable of (timestamp, acceleration, "
298	            "angular_velocity) triples"
299	        )
300	    try:
301	        raw_samples = list(imu_samples)  # type: ignore[call-overload]
302	    except TypeError:
303	        raise TypeError(
304	            "imu_samples must be an iterable of (timestamp, acceleration, "
305	            "angular_velocity) triples"
306	        ) from None
307	    if len(raw_samples) < 2:
308	        raise ValueError(
309	            f"imu_samples must contain at least two samples, got {len(raw_samples)}"
310	        )
311	    records = [_unpack_sample(sample, index) for index, sample in enumerate(raw_samples)]
312	
313	    if isinstance(pose_observations, (str, bytes, bytearray)):
314	        raise TypeError(
315	            "pose_observations must be an iterable of (timestamp, pose) pairs"
316	        )
317	    try:
318	        raw_observations = list(pose_observations)  # type: ignore[call-overload]
319	    except TypeError:
320	        raise TypeError(
321	            "pose_observations must be an iterable of (timestamp, pose) pairs"
322	        ) from None
323	    observations = [
324	        _unpack_observation(observation, index)
325	        for index, observation in enumerate(raw_observations)
326	    ]
327	
328	    previous_time: float | None = None
329	    for index, (timestamp, _, _) in enumerate(records):
330	        if previous_time is not None and timestamp <= previous_time:
331	            raise ValueError(
332	                "imu_samples timestamps must be strictly increasing, got "
333	                f"{previous_time!r} followed by {timestamp!r}"
334	            )
335	        previous_time = timestamp
336	
337	    previous_obs_time: float | None = None
338	    for index, (timestamp, _) in enumerate(observations):
339	        if previous_obs_time is not None and timestamp <= previous_obs_time:
340	            raise ValueError(
341	                "pose_observations timestamps must be strictly increasing, "
342	                f"got {previous_obs_time!r} followed by {timestamp!r}"
343	            )
344	        previous_obs_time = timestamp
345	
346	    imu_times = {timestamp for timestamp, _, _ in records}
347	    for timestamp, _ in observations:
348	        if timestamp not in imu_times:
349	            raise ValueError(
350	                f"pose observation timestamp {timestamp!r} does not match "
351	                "any IMU sample timestamp"
352	            )
353	    observations_by_time = {
354	        timestamp: observed_pose for timestamp, observed_pose in observations
355	    }
356	
357	    def apply_observation(
358	        predicted: Pose3, observed: Pose3
359	    ) -> tuple[Pose3, bool]:
360	        """Right-compose the gain-scaled residual, honoring the gate."""
361	        error = predicted.inverse().compose(observed)
362	        xi = error.log()
363	        if threshold is not None:
364	            translation_norm = math.hypot(*error.translation)
365	            rotation_norm = math.hypot(xi[0], xi[1], xi[2])
366	            if translation_norm > threshold or rotation_norm > threshold:
367	                return predicted, False
368	        scaled = (
369	            r_gain * xi[0],
370	            r_gain * xi[1],
371	            r_gain * xi[2],
372	            t_gain * xi[3],
373	            t_gain * xi[4],
374	            t_gain * xi[5],
375	        )
376	        return predicted.compose(Pose3.exp(scaled)), True
377	
378	    states: list[FusionState] = []
379	
380	    pose = initial_pose
381	    velocity = velocity0
382	    first_timestamp = records[0][0]
383	    first_observation = observations_by_time.get(first_timestamp)
384	    if first_observation is not None:
385	        # An observation at the first IMU time corrects the initial state;
386	        # the gate applies exactly as at any other time.
387	        pose, used = apply_observation(pose, first_observation)
388	        used_flag: bool | None = used
389	    else:
390	        used_flag = None
391	    states.append(FusionState(first_timestamp, pose, velocity, used_flag))
392	
393	    for index in range(1, len(records)):
394	        timestamp, acceleration, angular_velocity = records[index - 1]
395	        next_timestamp = records[index][0]
396	        dt = next_timestamp - timestamp
397	
398	        corrected_accel = (
399	            acceleration[0] - accel_bias[0],
400	            acceleration[1] - accel_bias[1],
401	            acceleration[2] - accel_bias[2],
402	        )
403	        corrected_omega = (
404	            angular_velocity[0] - gyro_bias[0],
405	            angular_velocity[1] - gyro_bias[1],
406	            angular_velocity[2] - gyro_bias[2],
407	        )
408	
409	        # Left-endpoint convention: the specific force is rotated with the
410	        # rotation at the beginning of the interval (rotation only -- the
411	        # pose translation must not enter the acceleration), while the
412	        # angular rate advances the rotation via right composition.
413	        r00, r01, r02 = pose.rotation[0]
414	        r10, r11, r12 = pose.rotation[1]
415	        r20, r21, r22 = pose.rotation[2]
416	        ax, ay, az = corrected_accel
417	        rotated_accel = (
418	            r00 * ax + r01 * ay + r02 * az,
419	            r10 * ax + r11 * ay + r12 * az,
420	            r20 * ax + r21 * ay + r22 * az,
421	        )
422	        accel_world = (
423	            rotated_accel[0] + gravity_vector[0],
424	            rotated_accel[1] + gravity_vector[1],
425	            rotated_accel[2] + gravity_vector[2],
426	        )
427	        half_dt_squared = 0.5 * dt * dt
428	        translation = pose.translation
429	        new_translation = (
430	            translation[0] + velocity[0] * dt + accel_world[0] * half_dt_squared,
431	            translation[1] + velocity[1] * dt + accel_world[1] * half_dt_squared,
432	            translation[2] + velocity[2] * dt + accel_world[2] * half_dt_squared,
433	        )
434	        new_velocity = (
435	            velocity[0] + accel_world[0] * dt,
436	            velocity[1] + accel_world[1] * dt,
437	            velocity[2] + accel_world[2] * dt,
438	        )
439	        rotation_step = Pose3.exp(
440	            (
441	                corrected_omega[0] * dt,
442	                corrected_omega[1] * dt,
443	                corrected_omega[2] * dt,
444	                0.0,
445	                0.0,
446	                0.0,
447	            )
448	        )
449	        new_rotation_pose = pose.compose(rotation_step)
450	        _finite_state(
451	            new_translation, new_rotation_pose.quaternion, new_velocity
452	        )
453	        pose = Pose3(new_translation, new_rotation_pose.quaternion)
454	        velocity = new_velocity
455	
456	        observation = observations_by_time.get(next_timestamp)
457	        if observation is None:
458	            used_flag = None
459	        else:
460	            pose, used = apply_observation(pose, observation)
461	            used_flag = used
462	        states.append(FusionState(next_timestamp, pose, velocity, used_flag))
463	
464	    return tuple(states)
465

__all__ = ["FusionState", "fuse_imu_pose"]

_ZERO_VECTOR = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)


class FusionState(NamedTuple):
    """Filter state at one IMU timestamp.

    Immutable. ``pose`` is the body-to-world :class:`~mappilot.geometry.Pose3`
    and ``velocity`` is the world-frame velocity after applying any
    observation at this timestamp. ``observation_used`` is ``None`` when no
    observation exists at this timestamp, ``True`` when one was applied,
    and ``False`` when one was present but rejected by the residual gate.
    """

    timestamp: float
    pose: Pose3
    velocity: tuple[float, float, float]
    observation_used: bool | None


def _real_scalar(value: object, name: str) -> float:
    """Coerce one real, non-boolean scalar to float (finiteness checked by caller)."""
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, numbers.Real):
        raise TypeError(f"{name} must be a real number, got {type(value).__name__}")
    return float(value)


def _finite_scalar(value: object, name: str) -> float:
    """Coerce one real, finite, non-boolean scalar to float."""
    result = _real_scalar(value, name)
    if not math.isfinite(result):
        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be finite, got {result!r}")
    return result


def _vector3(value: object, name: str) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
    """Validate one vector of exactly three finite, non-boolean real scalars."""
    if isinstance(value, (str, bytes, bytearray)):
        raise TypeError(f"{name} must be a sequence of 3 real numbers")
    try:
        items = tuple(value)  # type: ignore[call-overload]
    except TypeError:
        raise TypeError(f"{name} must be a sequence of 3 real numbers") from None
    if len(items) != 3:
        raise TypeError(f"{name} must have 3 elements, got {len(items)}")
    return (
        _finite_scalar(items[0], f"{name}[0]"),
        _finite_scalar(items[1], f"{name}[1]"),
        _finite_scalar(items[2], f"{name}[2]"),
    )


def _unpack_sample(
    sample: object, index: int
) -> tuple[float, tuple[float, float, float], tuple[float, float, float]]:
    """Validate one ``(timestamp, acceleration, angular_velocity)`` sample."""
    if isinstance(sample, (str, bytes, bytearray)):
        raise TypeError(
            f"imu_samples[{index}] must be a (timestamp, acceleration, "
            "angular_velocity) triple"
        )
    try:
        items = tuple(sample)  # type: ignore[call-overload]
    except TypeError:
        raise TypeError(
            f"imu_samples[{index}] must be a (timestamp, acceleration, "
            "angular_velocity) triple"
        ) from None
    if len(items) != 3:
        raise TypeError(
            f"imu_samples[{index}] must have exactly 3 elements "
            f"(timestamp, acceleration, angular_velocity), got {len(items)}"
        )
    timestamp = _finite_scalar(items[0], f"imu_samples[{index}][0]")
    acceleration = _vector3(items[1], f"imu_samples[{index}][1]")
    angular_velocity = _vector3(items[2], f"imu_samples[{index}][2]")
    return timestamp, acceleration, angular_velocity


def _unpack_observation(
    observation: object, index: int
) -> tuple[float, Pose3]:
    """Validate one ``(timestamp, pose)`` observation."""
    if isinstance(observation, (str, bytes, bytearray)):
        raise TypeError(
            f"pose_observations[{index}] must be a (timestamp, pose) pair"
        )
    try:
        items = tuple(observation)  # type: ignore[call-overload]
    except TypeError:
        raise TypeError(
            f"pose_observations[{index}] must be a (timestamp, pose) pair"
        ) from None
    if len(items) != 2:
        raise TypeError(
            f"pose_observations[{index}] must have exactly 2 elements "
            f"(timestamp, pose), got {len(items)}"
        )
    timestamp = _finite_scalar(items[0], f"pose_observations[{index}][0]")
    pose = items[1]
    if not isinstance(pose, Pose3):
        raise TypeError(
            f"pose_observations[{index}][1] must be a Pose3, got "
            f"{type(pose).__name__}"
        )
    return timestamp, pose


def _gain(value: object, name: str) -> float:
    """Validate one correction gain: a finite real in [0, 1]."""
    result = _real_scalar(value, name)
    if not math.isfinite(result):
        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be finite, got {result!r}")
    if not 0.0 <= result <= 1.0:
        raise ValueError(f"{name} must lie in [0, 1], got {result!r}")
    return result


def _threshold(value: object) -> float | None:
    """Validate an optional residual gate: ``None`` or a finite non-negative real."""
    if value is None:
        return None
    result = _real_scalar(value, "residual_threshold")
    if not math.isfinite(result):
        raise ValueError(f"residual_threshold must be finite, got {result!r}")
    if result < 0.0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"residual_threshold must be non-negative, got {result!r}"
        )
    return result


def _finite_state(
    translation: tuple[float, float, float],
    quaternion: tuple[float, float, float, float],
    velocity: tuple[float, float, float],
) -> None:
    for component in (*translation, *quaternion, *velocity):
        if not math.isfinite(component):
            raise ValueError("IMU propagation produced non-finite state")


def fuse_imu_pose(
    imu_samples: Iterable[
        tuple[float, tuple[float, float, float], tuple[float, float, float]]
    ],
    pose_observations: Iterable[tuple[float, Pose3]],
    initial_pose: Pose3,
    initial_velocity: Iterable[float],
    accelerometer_bias: Iterable[float] = _ZERO_VECTOR,
    gyroscope_bias: Iterable[float] = _ZERO_VECTOR,
    gravity: Iterable[float] = _ZERO_VECTOR,
    translation_gain: float = 1.0,
    rotation_gain: float = 1.0,
    residual_threshold: float | None = None,
) -> tuple[FusionState, ...]:
    """Fuse strapdown IMU propagation with timestamped pose observations.

    Parameters
    ----------
    imu_samples:
        ``(timestamp, acceleration, angular_velocity)`` records with
        strictly increasing absolute timestamps (seconds); at least two
        samples. The iterable is consumed exactly once.
    pose_observations:
        ``(timestamp, pose)`` pairs ordered by strictly increasing
        timestamps; the sequence may be empty. Each timestamp must equal an
        IMU timestamp exactly and no timestamp may repeat. The iterable is
        consumed exactly once.
    initial_pose:
        Body-to-world :class:`~mappilot.geometry.Pose3` at the first IMU
        timestamp.
    initial_velocity:
        World-frame velocity 3-vector at the first IMU timestamp.
    accelerometer_bias, gyroscope_bias:
        Constant body-frame 3-vector biases subtracted from the
        acceleration and angular-rate measurements; zero by default.
    gravity:
        World-frame gravity 3-vector added to the rotated specific force;
        zero by default.
    translation_gain, rotation_gain:
        Gains in ``[0, 1]`` scaling the translation and rotation parts of
        each applied correction; 1.0 by default (full correction).
    residual_threshold:
        ``None`` (default, no gating) or a non-negative finite bound; an
        observation is rejected when the residual translation norm or
        rotation norm is strictly greater than it. Equality is accepted.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[FusionState, ...]
        One immutable :class:`FusionState` per IMU sample, in timestamp
        order, each carrying the pose (and world velocity) after any
        observation at that timestamp. ``observation_used`` is ``None``
        without an observation, ``True`` when one was applied, and
        ``False`` when the gate rejected one.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        Non-iterable inputs or records, malformed records, wrong vector
        dimensions, non-real or boolean values, an ``initial_pose`` or
        observed pose that is not a :class:`~mappilot.geometry.Pose3`, or
        gains/threshold of the wrong numeric type.
    ValueError
        Fewer than two IMU samples; non-finite values; timestamps that are
        not strictly increasing in either sequence; an observation
        timestamp missing from the IMU timeline; a gain outside ``[0, 1]``;
        a negative or non-finite threshold; or non-finite propagation
        results.
    """
    if not isinstance(initial_pose, Pose3):
        raise TypeError(
            f"initial_pose must be a Pose3, got {type(initial_pose).__name__}"
        )
    velocity0 = _vector3(initial_velocity, "initial_velocity")
    accel_bias = _vector3(accelerometer_bias, "accelerometer_bias")
    gyro_bias = _vector3(gyroscope_bias, "gyroscope_bias")
    gravity_vector = _vector3(gravity, "gravity")
    t_gain = _gain(translation_gain, "translation_gain")
    r_gain = _gain(rotation_gain, "rotation_gain")
    threshold = _threshold(residual_threshold)

    # Materialize both iterables exactly once; validated records are freshly
    # built floats and Pose3 values are immutable, so caller objects are
    # never mutated or aliased into mutable state.
    if isinstance(imu_samples, (str, bytes, bytearray)):
        raise TypeError(
            "imu_samples must be an iterable of (timestamp, acceleration, "
            "angular_velocity) triples"
        )
    try:
        raw_samples = list(imu_samples)  # type: ignore[call-overload]
    except TypeError:
        raise TypeError(
            "imu_samples must be an iterable of (timestamp, acceleration, "
            "angular_velocity) triples"
        ) from None
    if len(raw_samples) < 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"imu_samples must contain at least two samples, got {len(raw_samples)}"
        )
    records = [_unpack_sample(sample, index) for index, sample in enumerate(raw_samples)]

    if isinstance(pose_observations, (str, bytes, bytearray)):
        raise TypeError(
            "pose_observations must be an iterable of (timestamp, pose) pairs"
        )
    try:
        raw_observations = list(pose_observations)  # type: ignore[call-overload]
    except TypeError:
        raise TypeError(
            "pose_observations must be an iterable of (timestamp, pose) pairs"
        ) from None
    observations = [
        _unpack_observation(observation, index)
        for index, observation in enumerate(raw_observations)
    ]

    previous_time: float | None = None
    for index, (timestamp, _, _) in enumerate(records):
        if previous_time is not None and timestamp <= previous_time:
            raise ValueError(
                "imu_samples timestamps must be strictly increasing, got "
                f"{previous_time!r} followed by {timestamp!r}"
            )
        previous_time = timestamp

    previous_obs_time: float | None = None
    for index, (timestamp, _) in enumerate(observations):
        if previous_obs_time is not None and timestamp <= previous_obs_time:
            raise ValueError(
                "pose_observations timestamps must be strictly increasing, "
                f"got {previous_obs_time!r} followed by {timestamp!r}"
            )
        previous_obs_time = timestamp

    imu_times = {timestamp for timestamp, _, _ in records}
    for timestamp, _ in observations:
        if timestamp not in imu_times:
            raise ValueError(
                f"pose observation timestamp {timestamp!r} does not match "
                "any IMU sample timestamp"
            )
    observations_by_time = {
        timestamp: observed_pose for timestamp, observed_pose in observations
    }

    def apply_observation(
        predicted: Pose3, observed: Pose3
    ) -> tuple[Pose3, bool]:
        """Right-compose the gain-scaled residual, honoring the gate."""
        error = predicted.inverse().compose(observed)
        xi = error.log()
        if threshold is not None:
            translation_norm = math.hypot(*error.translation)
            rotation_norm = math.hypot(xi[0], xi[1], xi[2])
            if translation_norm > threshold or rotation_norm > threshold:
                return predicted, False
        scaled = (
            r_gain * xi[0],
            r_gain * xi[1],
            r_gain * xi[2],
            t_gain * xi[3],
            t_gain * xi[4],
            t_gain * xi[5],
        )
        return predicted.compose(Pose3.exp(scaled)), True

    states: list[FusionState] = []

    pose = initial_pose
    velocity = velocity0
    first_timestamp = records[0][0]
    first_observation = observations_by_time.get(first_timestamp)
    if first_observation is not None:
        # An observation at the first IMU time corrects the initial state;
        # the gate applies exactly as at any other time.
        pose, used = apply_observation(pose, first_observation)
        used_flag: bool | None = used
    else:
        used_flag = None
    states.append(FusionState(first_timestamp, pose, velocity, used_flag))

    for index in range(1, len(records)):
        timestamp, acceleration, angular_velocity = records[index - 1]
        next_timestamp = records[index][0]
        dt = next_timestamp - timestamp

        corrected_accel = (
            acceleration[0] - accel_bias[0],
            acceleration[1] - accel_bias[1],
            acceleration[2] - accel_bias[2],
        )
        corrected_omega = (
            angular_velocity[0] - gyro_bias[0],
            angular_velocity[1] - gyro_bias[1],
            angular_velocity[2] - gyro_bias[2],
        )

        # Left-endpoint convention: the specific force is rotated with the
        # rotation at the beginning of the interval (rotation only -- the
        # pose translation must not enter the acceleration), while the
        # angular rate advances the rotation via right composition.
        r00, r01, r02 = pose.rotation[0]
        r10, r11, r12 = pose.rotation[1]
        r20, r21, r22 = pose.rotation[2]
        ax, ay, az = corrected_accel
        rotated_accel = (
            r00 * ax + r01 * ay + r02 * az,
            r10 * ax + r11 * ay + r12 * az,
            r20 * ax + r21 * ay + r22 * az,
        )
        accel_world = (
            rotated_accel[0] + gravity_vector[0],
            rotated_accel[1] + gravity_vector[1],
            rotated_accel[2] + gravity_vector[2],
        )
        half_dt_squared = 0.5 * dt * dt
        translation = pose.translation
        new_translation = (
            translation[0] + velocity[0] * dt + accel_world[0] * half_dt_squared,
            translation[1] + velocity[1] * dt + accel_world[1] * half_dt_squared,
            translation[2] + velocity[2] * dt + accel_world[2] * half_dt_squared,
        )
        new_velocity = (
            velocity[0] + accel_world[0] * dt,
            velocity[1] + accel_world[1] * dt,
            velocity[2] + accel_world[2] * dt,
        )
        rotation_step = Pose3.exp(
            (
                corrected_omega[0] * dt,
                corrected_omega[1] * dt,
                corrected_omega[2] * dt,
                0.0,
                0.0,
                0.0,
            )
        )
        new_rotation_pose = pose.compose(rotation_step)
        _finite_state(
            new_translation, new_rotation_pose.quaternion, new_velocity
        )
        pose = Pose3(new_translation, new_rotation_pose.quaternion)
        velocity = new_velocity

        observation = observations_by_time.get(next_timestamp)
        if observation is None:
            used_flag = None
        else:
            pose, used = apply_observation(pose, observation)
            used_flag = used
        states.append(FusionState(next_timestamp, pose, velocity, used_flag))

    return tuple(states)

1	"""Pose-graph optimization over SE(3) relative-pose constraints.
2	
3	The :func:`optimize_pose_graph` entry point takes an ordered, uniquely
4	identified sequence of :class:`~mappilot.geometry.Pose3` node initial values
5	and a sequence of relative-pose constraints, and produces a globally
6	consistent trajectory by Gauss-Newton iteration.
7	
8	For every constraint ``(i, j, z, Omega)`` the residual is
9	
10	    e = log( z^{-1} * T_i^{-1} * T_j )
11	
12	(a 6D tangent vector ordered like :meth:`Pose3.log`:
13	``(wx, wy, wz, vx, vy, vz)``) and the total error is the sum of quadratic
14	forms ``e^T Omega e``. ``Omega`` must be a symmetric positive-definite 6x6
15	matrix whose entries align with the :meth:`Pose3.log` components.
16	
17	Each Gauss-Newton step linearizes the residual under the left-perturbation
18	convention used by :meth:`Pose3.exp`/:meth:`Pose3.log` (``T <- exp(dx) T``):
19	
20	    J_j =  J_l(e)^{-1} Ad_{z^{-1} T_i^{-1}}
21	    J_i = -J_j
22	
23	solves the reduced normal equations (rows and columns of fixed nodes
24	eliminated) by pivoted Gaussian elimination, and applies the update
25	simultaneously to every free node. Fixed node poses are never touched, so
26	disconnected components are optimized independently as long as each
27	component carries at least one fixed node.
28	
29	This module is pure Python and depends only on the standard library plus
30	:mod:`mappilot.geometry`. Importing it never starts the HTTP service.
31	
32	Validation policy mirrors :mod:`mappilot.geometry` and
33	:mod:`mappilot.registration`: non-iterable inputs, non-integer (including
34	boolean) node ids, non-:class:`Pose3` poses, malformed constraint tuples or
35	information matrices, non-real (including boolean) matrix entries, and
36	parameters of the wrong type raise :class:`TypeError`; empty or duplicate
37	node ids, constraints referencing unknown nodes, unknown or empty fixed
38	sets, connected components without a fixed node, non-finite matrix
39	entries, information matrices that are not symmetric (absolute tolerance
40	1e-12) or not positive definite, and non-positive or non-finite
41	``max_iterations``/``tolerance`` raise :class:`ValueError`.
42	"""
43	
44	from __future__ import annotations
45	
46	import math
47	import numbers
48	from typing import Iterable, NamedTuple
49	
50	from .geometry import Pose3
51	
52	__all__ = ["PoseGraphResult", "optimize_pose_graph"]
53	
54	_DOF = 6
55	
56	# Information-matrix symmetry tolerance.
57	_SYMMETRY_TOL = 1e-12
58	
59	# Terms of the SE(3) left-Jacobian power series (ad_x^n / (n+1)!). With the
60	# log angle in [0, pi] the tail past n=24 is below ~1e-12 in exact
61	# arithmetic; 24 leaves a wide safety margin in double precision.
62	_JACOBIAN_TERMS = 24
63	
64	
65	class PoseGraphResult(NamedTuple):
66	    """Outcome of :func:`optimize_pose_graph`.
67	
68	    Immutable. ``nodes`` holds ``(id, pose)`` pairs in exactly the order the
69	    nodes were supplied; fixed node poses are the input objects, unchanged
70	    value by value. ``initial_error`` and ``final_error`` are recomputed from
71	    the corresponding poses, so they always agree with ``nodes``.
72	    """
73	
74	    nodes: tuple[tuple[int, Pose3], ...]
75	    converged: bool
76	    iterations: int
77	    initial_error: float
78	    final_error: float
79

84	def _node_id(value: object, name: str) -> int:
85	    """Coerce one non-boolean integral node id to int."""
86	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, numbers.Integral):
87	        raise TypeError(f"{name} must be an integer node id, got {type(value).__name__}")
88	    return int(value)
89	
90	
91	def _positive_int(value: object, name: str) -> int:
92	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, numbers.Integral):
93	        raise TypeError(f"{name} must be an integer, got {type(value).__name__}")
94	    result = int(value)
95	    if result < 1:
96	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a positive integer, got {result}")
97	    return result
98	
99	
100	def _positive_float(value: object, name: str) -> float:
101	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, numbers.Real):
102	        raise TypeError(f"{name} must be a real number, got {type(value).__name__}")
103	    result = float(value)
104	    if not math.isfinite(result):
105	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be finite, got {result!r}")
106	    if result <= 0.0:
107	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be greater than zero, got {result}")
108	    return result
109	
110	
111	def _matrix_entry(value: object, name: str) -> float:
112	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, numbers.Real):
113	        raise TypeError(f"{name} must be a real number, got {type(value).__name__}")
114	    result = float(value)
115	    if not math.isfinite(result):
116	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be finite, got {result!r}")

120	def _pair(value: object, name: str, length: int) -> tuple:
121	    """Materialize one fixed-length input tuple; type-error on bad shape."""
122	    if isinstance(value, (str, bytes, bytearray)):
123	        raise TypeError(f"{name} must be a sequence of {length} elements")
124	    try:
125	        items = tuple(value)  # type: ignore[call-overload]
126	    except TypeError:
127	        raise TypeError(f"{name} must be a sequence of {length} elements") from None
128	    if len(items) != length:
129	        raise TypeError(f"{name} must have exactly {length} elements, got {len(items)}")
130	    return items

133	# -- information matrix ------------------------------------------------------
134	
135	
136	def _information_matrix(value: object) -> tuple[tuple[float, ...], ...]:
137	    """Validate a symmetric positive-definite 6x6 real matrix."""
138	    if isinstance(value, (str, bytes, bytearray)):
139	        raise TypeError("information must be a 6x6 nested sequence of real numbers")
140	    try:
141	        rows = tuple(value)  # type: ignore[call-overload]
142	    except TypeError:
143	        raise TypeError("information must be a 6x6 nested sequence of real numbers") from None
144	    if len(rows) != _DOF:
145	        raise TypeError(f"information must have {_DOF} rows, got {len(rows)}")
146	
147	    grid: list[tuple[float, ...]] = []
148	    for row_index, row in enumerate(rows):
149	        if isinstance(row, (str, bytes, bytearray)):
150	            raise TypeError(f"information[{row_index}] must be a sequence of 6 real numbers")
151	        try:
152	            items = tuple(row)  # type: ignore[call-overload]
153	        except TypeError:
154	            raise TypeError(
155	                f"information[{row_index}] must be a sequence of 6 real numbers"
156	            ) from None
157	        if len(items) != _DOF:
158	            raise TypeError(
159	                f"information[{row_index}] must have {_DOF} elements, got {len(items)}"
160	            )
161	        grid.append(
162	            tuple(
163	                _matrix_entry(item, f"information[{row_index}][{col_index}]")
164	                for col_index, item in enumerate(items)
165	            )
166	        )
167	
168	    matrix = tuple(grid)
169	    for i in range(_DOF):
170	        for j in range(i + 1, _DOF):
171	            if abs(matrix[i][j] - matrix[j][i]) > _SYMMETRY_TOL:
172	                raise ValueError("information matrix must be symmetric")
173	
174	    # Positive definiteness via symmetric Gaussian elimination (LDL^T without
175	    # pivoting): a symmetric matrix is positive definite iff every pivot is
176	    # positive. A symmetric positive-definite matrix never needs pivoting.
177	    work = [list(row) for row in matrix]
178	    for k in range(_DOF):
179	        pivot = work[k][k]
180	        if pivot <= 0.0:
181	            raise ValueError("information matrix must be positive definite")
182	        for i in range(k + 1, _DOF):
183	            factor = work[i][k] / pivot
184	            if factor == 0.0:
185	                continue
186	            for j in range(k + 1, _DOF):
187	                work[i][j] -= factor * work[k][j]
188	    return matrix

194	def _parse_nodes(
195	    value: object,
196	) -> tuple[tuple[tuple[int, Pose3], ...], dict[int, int]]:
197	    """Validate the ordered node sequence; return pairs and id->index."""
198	    if isinstance(value, (str, bytes, bytearray)):
199	        raise TypeError("nodes must be an iterable of (id, pose) pairs")
200	    try:
201	        raw_nodes = tuple(value)  # type: ignore[call-overload]
202	    except TypeError:
203	        raise TypeError("nodes must be an iterable of (id, pose) pairs") from None
204	    if len(raw_nodes) == 0:
205	        raise ValueError("nodes must not be empty")
206	
207	    nodes: list[tuple[int, Pose3]] = []
208	    index_by_id: dict[int, int] = {}
209	    for position, raw_node in enumerate(raw_nodes):
210	        items = _pair(raw_node, f"nodes[{position}]", 2)
211	        node_id = _node_id(items[0], f"nodes[{position}][0]")
212	        pose = items[1]
213	        if not isinstance(pose, Pose3):
214	            raise TypeError(
215	                f"nodes[{position}][1] must be a Pose3, got {type(pose).__name__}"
216	            )
217	        if node_id in index_by_id:
218	            raise ValueError(f"duplicate node id: {node_id}")
219	        index_by_id[node_id] = position
220	        nodes.append((node_id, pose))
221	    return tuple(nodes), index_by_id

224	def _parse_constraints(
225	    value: object, index_by_id: dict[int, int]
226	) -> tuple[tuple[int, int, Pose3, tuple[tuple[float, ...], ...]], ...]:
227	    """Validate ``(from_id, to_id, measurement, information)`` constraints."""
228	    if isinstance(value, (str, bytes, bytearray)):
229	        raise TypeError(
230	            "constraints must be an iterable of "
231	            "(from_id, to_id, measurement, information) tuples"
232	        )
233	    try:
234	        raw_constraints = tuple(value)  # type: ignore[call-overload]
235	    except TypeError:
236	        raise TypeError(
237	            "constraints must be an iterable of "
238	            "(from_id, to_id, measurement, information) tuples"
239	        ) from None
240	
241	    constraints: list[tuple[int, int, Pose3, tuple[tuple[float, ...], ...]]] = []
242	    for position, raw_constraint in enumerate(raw_constraints):
243	        name = f"constraints[{position}]"
244	        items = _pair(
245	            raw_constraint,
246	            name,
247	            4,
248	        )
249	        from_id = _node_id(items[0], f"{name}[0]")
250	        to_id = _node_id(items[1], f"{name}[1]")
251	        measurement = items[2]
252	        if not isinstance(measurement, Pose3):
253	            raise TypeError(
254	                f"{name}[2] must be a Pose3, got {type(measurement).__name__}"
255	            )
256	        information = _information_matrix(items[3])
257	        if from_id not in index_by_id:
258	            raise ValueError(f"{name} references unknown node id: {from_id}")
259	        if to_id not in index_by_id:
260	            raise ValueError(f"{name} references unknown node id: {to_id}")
261	        constraints.append(
262	            (index_by_id[from_id], index_by_id[to_id], measurement, information)
263	        )
264	    return tuple(constraints)
265	
266	
267	def _parse_fixed(value: object, index_by_id: dict[int, int]) -> frozenset[int]:
268	    if isinstance(value, (str, bytes, bytearray)):
269	        raise TypeError("fixed_node_ids must be an iterable of integer node ids")
270	    try:
271	        raw_ids = tuple(value)  # type: ignore[call-overload]
272	    except TypeError:
273	        raise TypeError("fixed_node_ids must be an iterable of integer node ids") from None
274	    fixed: set[int] = set()
275	    for position, raw_id in enumerate(raw_ids):
276	        node_id = _node_id(raw_id, f"fixed_node_ids[{position}]")
277	        if node_id not in index_by_id:
278	            raise ValueError(f"fixed node id is unknown: {node_id}")
279	        fixed.add(index_by_id[node_id])
280	    if not fixed:
281	        raise ValueError("fixed_node_ids must not be empty")
282	    return frozenset(fixed)
283	
284	
285	def _check_components(
286	    node_count: int,
287	    constraints: tuple[tuple[int, int, Pose3, tuple[tuple[float, ...], ...]], ...],
288	    fixed: frozenset[int],
289	) -> None:
290	    """Raise if any undirected connected component lacks a fixed node."""
291	    adjacency: list[list[int]] = [[] for _ in range(node_count)]
292	    for from_index, to_index, _, _ in constraints:
293	        adjacency[from_index].append(to_index)
294	        adjacency[to_index].append(from_index)
295	
296	    seen = [False] * node_count
297	    for start in range(node_count):
298	        if seen[start]:
299	            continue
300	        seen[start] = True
301	        stack = [start]
302	        component_has_fixed = start in fixed
303	        while stack:
304	            node = stack.pop()
305	            for neighbour in adjacency[node]:
306	                if not seen[neighbour]:
307	                    seen[neighbour] = True
308	                    if neighbour in fixed:
309	                        component_has_fixed = True
310	                    stack.append(neighbour)
311	        if not component_has_fixed:
312	            raise ValueError(
313	                "every connected component must contain at least one fixed node; "
314	                f"the component containing node index {start} has none"
315	            )
316	
317	
318	# -- small dense linear algebra (standard library only) ----------------------
319	
320	
321	def _mat_mul(a, b):
322	    """Product of two square matrices stored as tuples of tuples."""
323	    size = len(a)
324	    return tuple(
325	        tuple(sum(a[i][k] * b[k][j] for k in range(size)) for j in range(size))
326	        for i in range(size)
327	    )
328	
329	
330	def _mat_vec_mul(matrix, vector):
331	    size = len(matrix)
332	    return tuple(
333	        sum(matrix[i][k] * vector[k] for k in range(size)) for i in range(size)
334	    )
335	
336	
337	def _identity(size: int):
338	    return tuple(
339	        tuple(1.0 if i == j else 0.0 for j in range(size)) for i in range(size)
340	    )
341	
342	
343	def _solve_linear(matrix, rhs):
344	    """Solve ``A x = b`` by Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting.
345	
346	    Returns a list. Raises :class:`ValueError` if the system is singular to
347	    working precision.
348	    """
349	    size = len(matrix)
350	    augmented = [list(matrix[i]) + [rhs[i]] for i in range(size)]
351	    for column in range(size):
352	        pivot = column
353	        for row in range(column + 1, size):
354	            if abs(augmented[row][column]) > abs(augmented[pivot][column]):
355	                pivot = row
356	        if augmented[pivot][column] == 0.0 or not math.isfinite(
357	            augmented[pivot][column]
358	        ):
359	            raise ValueError("linear system is singular")
360	        if pivot != column:
361	            augmented[column], augmented[pivot] = augmented[pivot], augmented[column]
362	        pivot_value = augmented[column][column]
363	        for row in range(column + 1, size):
364	            factor = augmented[row][column] / pivot_value
365	            if factor == 0.0:
366	                continue
367	            for col in range(column, size + 1):
368	                augmented[row][col] -= factor * augmented[column][col]
369	    solution = [0.0] * size
370	    for row in range(size - 1, -1, -1):
371	        total = augmented[row][size]
372	        for col in range(row + 1, size):
373	            total -= augmented[row][col] * solution[col]
374	        solution[row] = total / augmented[row][row]
375	    return solution
376	
377	
378	def _invert_matrix(matrix):
379	    """Invert a non-singular square matrix by solving against identity cols."""
380	    size = len(matrix)
381	    columns = []
382	    for basis in range(size):
383	        rhs = [0.0] * size
384	        rhs[basis] = 1.0
385	        columns.append(_solve_linear(matrix, rhs))
386	    return tuple(
387	        tuple(columns[j][i] for j in range(size)) for i in range(size)
388	    )
389	
390	
391	# -- SE(3) adjoint and left Jacobian -----------------------------------------
392	
393	
394	def _skew3(x: float, y: float, z: float):
395	    return (
396	        (0.0, -z, y),
397	        (z, 0.0, -x),
398	        (-y, x, 0.0),
399	    )
400	
401	
402	def _adjoint(pose: Pose3):
403	    """``Ad_T = [[R, 0], [[t]x R, R]]`` in tangent order (omega, v)."""
404	    rotation = pose.rotation
405	    tx, ty, tz = pose.translation
406	    skew_t = _skew3(tx, ty, tz)
407	    bottom = tuple(
408	        tuple(
409	            sum(skew_t[row][k] * rotation[k][col] for k in range(3))
410	            for col in range(3)
411	        )
412	        for row in range(3)
413	    )
414	    return (
415	        (rotation[0][0], rotation[0][1], rotation[0][2], 0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
416	        (rotation[1][0], rotation[1][1], rotation[1][2], 0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
417	        (rotation[2][0], rotation[2][1], rotation[2][2], 0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
418	        (bottom[0][0], bottom[0][1], bottom[0][2],
419	         rotation[0][0], rotation[0][1], rotation[0][2]),
420	        (bottom[1][0], bottom[1][1], bottom[1][2],
421	         rotation[1][0], rotation[1][1], rotation[1][2]),
422	        (bottom[2][0], bottom[2][1], bottom[2][2],
423	         rotation[2][0], rotation[2][1], rotation[2][2]),
424	    )
425	
426	
427	def _se3_adjoint_algebra(xi):
428	    """6x6 matrix ``ad_xi`` for ``xi = (wx, wy, wz, vx, vy, vz)``.
429	
430	    Block form ``[[w]x, 0; [v]x, [w]x]``; the left-Jacobian series
431	    ``sum ad_xi^n / (n+1)!`` is built from this matrix.
432	    """
433	    wx, wy, wz, vx, vy, vz = xi
434	    kw = _skew3(wx, wy, wz)
435	    kv = _skew3(vx, vy, vz)
436	    return (
437	        (kw[0][0], kw[0][1], kw[0][2], 0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
438	        (kw[1][0], kw[1][1], kw[1][2], 0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
439	        (kw[2][0], kw[2][1], kw[2][2], 0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
440	        (kv[0][0], kv[0][1], kv[0][2], kw[0][0], kw[0][1], kw[0][2]),
441	        (kv[1][0], kv[1][1], kv[1][2], kw[1][0], kw[1][1], kw[1][2]),
442	        (kv[2][0], kv[2][1], kv[2][2], kw[2][0], kw[2][1], kw[2][2]),
443	    )
444	
445	
446	def _inverse_left_jacobian(xi):
447	    """``J_l(xi)^{-1}`` as a 6x6 matrix.
448	
449	    ``J_l(xi) = sum_{n>=0} ad_xi^n / (n+1)!`` evaluated by Horner's rule,
450	    then inverted by pivoted Gaussian elimination. :meth:`Pose3.log` bounds
451	    the rotation angle by pi, well inside the series' convergence radius of
452	    2*pi, so the truncated tail is negligible.
453	    """
454	    ad = _se3_adjoint_algebra(xi)
455	    identity = _identity(_DOF)
456	    series = identity
457	    # J = I + ad/2 (I + ad/3 (I + ... + ad/(TERMS+1) I ...))
458	    for divisor in range(_JACOBIAN_TERMS + 1, 1, -1):
459	        scaled = tuple(
460	            tuple(ad[i][j] / divisor for j in range(_DOF)) for i in range(_DOF)
461	        )
462	        series = tuple(
463	            tuple(
464	                identity[i][j] + sum(scaled[i][k] * series[k][j] for k in range(_DOF))
465	                for j in range(_DOF)
466	            )
467	            for i in range(_DOF)
468	        )
469	    return _invert_matrix(series)
470	
471	
472	# -- residual / error ---------------------------------------------------------
473	
474	
475	def _residual_and_jacobians(
476	    pose_from: Pose3, pose_to: Pose3, measurement: Pose3
477	):
478	    """Return ``(e, J_from, J_to)`` for one constraint ``log(z^-1 Ti^-1 Tj)``.
479	
480	    Left perturbation ``T <- exp(d) T`` gives (see module docstring)::
481	
482	        J_to   =  J_l(e)^{-1} Ad_{z^{-1} T_i^{-1}}
483	        J_from = -J_to
484	    """
485	    error_pose = measurement.inverse().compose(
486	        pose_from.inverse().compose(pose_to)
487	    )
488	    residual = error_pose.log()
489	    base = _mat_mul(
490	        _inverse_left_jacobian(residual),
491	        _adjoint(measurement.inverse().compose(pose_from.inverse())),
492	    )
493	    j_from = tuple(tuple(-value for value in row) for row in base)
494	    return residual, j_from, base
495	
496	
497	def _quadratic_form(information, residual) -> float:
498	    total = 0.0
499	    for i in range(_DOF):
500	        weighted = sum(information[i][k] * residual[k] for k in range(_DOF))
501	        total += residual[i] * weighted
502	    return total
503	
504	
505	def _total_error(poses, constraints) -> float:
506	    total = 0.0
507	    for from_index, to_index, measurement, information in constraints:
508	        residual = measurement.inverse().compose(
509	            poses[from_index].inverse().compose(poses[to_index])
510	        ).log()
511	        total += _quadratic_form(information, residual)
512	    return total
513	
514	
515	# -- public entry point -------------------------------------------------------
516	
517	
518	def optimize_pose_graph(
519	    nodes: Iterable[tuple[int, Pose3]],
520	    constraints: Iterable[tuple[int, Pose3, Pose3, tuple[tuple[float, ...], ...]]],
521	    fixed_node_ids: Iterable[int],
522	    max_iterations: int = 50,
523	    tolerance: float = 1e-6,
524	) -> PoseGraphResult:
525	    """Optimize a pose graph of :class:`~mappilot.geometry.Pose3` nodes.
526	
527	    Parameters
528	    ----------
529	    nodes:
530	        Ordered sequence of unique ``(id, pose)`` pairs; ``id`` is a
531	        non-boolean integer and ``pose`` a :class:`~mappilot.geometry.Pose3`
532	        used as the Gauss-Newton initial value.
533	    constraints:
534	        Sequence of ``(from_id, to_id, measurement, information)`` tuples.
535	        ``measurement`` is the measured relative pose from the ``from`` node
536	        to the ``to`` node; ``information`` is a symmetric positive-definite
537	        6x6 matrix aligned with :meth:`Pose3.log` components.
538	    fixed_node_ids:
539	        Non-empty iterable of node ids held exactly at their input poses.
540	        Every connected component must contain at least one fixed node.
541	    max_iterations:
542	        Maximum number of Gauss-Newton updates; positive integer, default 50.
543	    tolerance:
544	        Finite positive convergence threshold on the absolute change in total
545	        error between consecutive updates, default 1e-6.
546	
547	    Returns
548	    -------
549	    PoseGraphResult
550	        If the initial total error is already at most ``tolerance``, the
551	        result reports ``converged=True`` with ``iterations=0`` and the input
552	        poses untouched. Otherwise the loop stops as soon as the absolute
553	        error change between two updates is at most ``tolerance``
554	        (``converged=True``), or after ``max_iterations`` updates with
555	        ``converged=False``. ``initial_error`` and ``final_error`` are
556	        recomputed from the corresponding poses; fixed node poses compare
557	        equal to the inputs value by value.
558	    """
559	    parsed_nodes, index_by_id = _parse_nodes(nodes)
560	    parsed_constraints = _parse_constraints(constraints, index_by_id)
561	    fixed_indices = _parse_fixed(fixed_node_ids, index_by_id)
562	    iteration_limit = _positive_int(max_iterations, "max_iterations")
563	    convergence_tolerance = _positive_float(tolerance, "tolerance")
564	    _check_components(len(parsed_nodes), parsed_constraints, fixed_indices)
565	
566	    node_ids = tuple(node_id for node_id, _ in parsed_nodes)
567	    poses: list[Pose3] = [pose for _, pose in parsed_nodes]
568	
569	    initial_error = _total_error(poses, parsed_constraints)
570	    if initial_error <= tolerance:
571	        return PoseGraphResult(
572	            tuple(zip(node_ids, poses)),
573	            True,
574	            0,
575	            initial_error,
576	            _total_error(poses, parsed_constraints),
577	        )
578	
579	    free_nodes = [i for i in range(len(poses)) if i not in fixed_indices]
580	    free_slot = {node_index: slot for slot, node_index in enumerate(free_nodes)}
581	    free_count = len(free_nodes)
582	
583	    converged = False
584	    iterations = 0
585	    previous_error = initial_error
586	
587	    for _ in range(iteration_limit):
588	        hessian = [[0.0] * (free_count * _DOF) for _ in range(free_count * _DOF)]
589	        gradient = [0.0] * (free_count * _DOF)
590	
591	        for from_index, to_index, measurement, information in parsed_constraints:
592	            residual, j_from, j_to = _residual_and_jacobians(
593	                poses[from_index], poses[to_index], measurement
594	            )
595	            weighted_error = _mat_vec_mul(information, residual)
596	
597	            for node_index, jacobian in (
598	                (from_index, j_from),
599	                (to_index, j_to),
600	            ):
601	                if node_index in fixed_indices:
602	                    continue
603	                slot = free_slot[node_index]
604	                for row in range(_DOF):
605	                    gradient[slot * _DOF + row] -= sum(
606	                        jacobian[k][row] * weighted_error[k] for k in range(_DOF)
607	                    )
608	
609	            blocks = ((from_index, j_from), (to_index, j_to))
610	            for node_a, jac_a in blocks:
611	                if node_a in fixed_indices:
612	                    continue
613	                slot_a = free_slot[node_a]
614	                for node_b, jac_b in blocks:
615	                    if node_b in fixed_indices:
616	                        continue
617	                    slot_b = free_slot[node_b]
618	                    for row in range(_DOF):
619	                        target = hessian[slot_a * _DOF + row]
620	                        base = slot_b * _DOF
621	                        for col in range(_DOF):
622	                            target[base + col] += sum(
623	                                jac_a[k][row] * information[k][k2] * jac_b[k2][col]
624	                                for k in range(_DOF) for k2 in range(_DOF)
625	                            )
626	
627	        # Gauss-Newton step: H dx = -J^T Omega e; apply T <- exp(dx) T.
628	        step = _solve_linear(hessian, gradient)
629	        for slot, node_index in enumerate(free_nodes):
630	            delta = tuple(step[slot * _DOF + k] for k in range(_DOF))
631	            poses[node_index] = Pose3.exp(delta).compose(poses[node_index])
632	        iterations += 1
633	
634	        current_error = _total_error(poses, parsed_constraints)
635	        if abs(previous_error - current_error) <= convergence_tolerance:
636	            converged = True
637	            previous_error = current_error
638	            break
639	        previous_error = current_error
640	
641	    return PoseGraphResult(
642	        tuple(zip(node_ids, poses)),
643	        converged,
644	        iterations,
645	        initial_error,
646	        _total_error(poses, parsed_constraints),
647	    )

1	"""Motion compensation (de-skewing) for one timestamped laser scan.
2	
3	A spinning or scanning LiDAR integrates a frame over time: each beam is
4	measured at a slightly different instant, so points taken from a moving
5	platform are skewed in space. :func:`deskew_point_cloud` undoes that skew by
6	re-expressing every point as if all beams had fired at one reference instant.
7	
8	The inputs follow the :mod:`mappilot.geometry` convention that a pose maps
9	local coordinates to parent coordinates
10	(``p_parent = R * p_local + t``):
11	
12	* ``trajectory`` samples are ``(time, Pose3)`` pairs; each :class:`Pose3`
13	  maps body coordinates to world coordinates at an absolute timestamp.
14	* ``sensor_to_body`` maps sensor coordinates to body coordinates.
15	* Each scan record holds the beam time as a seconds offset relative to
16	  ``scan_time`` and one 3D point in sensor coordinates.
17	
18	For a beam fired at ``tau`` the body pose is interpolated from the two
19	trajectory samples bracketing ``tau``: translation componentwise linear,
20	rotation along the unit-quaternion shortest arc. A point whose time lands
21	exactly on a sample uses that sample directly. The point is transformed to
22	the world frame through the interpolated body pose and ``sensor_to_body``,
23	then pulled into the sensor frame at ``reference_time`` through the inverse
24	of that frame's sensor-to-world pose:
25	
26	``p_ref = T_sensor_world(ref)^{-1} * T_body_world(tau)
27	          * T_sensor_body * p``.
28	
29	This module is pure Python and depends only on the standard library plus
30	:mod:`mappilot.geometry`. Importing it never starts the HTTP service.
31	
32	Validation policy mirrors :mod:`mappilot.geometry`: non-real scalars
33	(including booleans), non-iterable inputs, malformed records, wrong point
34	dimensions, and trajectory poses or extrinsics that are not :class:`Pose3`
35	raise :class:`TypeError`; empty point clouds, trajectories with fewer than
36	two samples, duplicate or out-of-order timestamps, non-finite values, points
37	or ``reference_time`` outside the trajectory's closed time interval, and an
38	interpolation span longer than ``max_interpolation_gap`` raise
39	:class:`ValueError`.
40	"""
41	
42	from __future__ import annotations
43	
44	import math
45	import numbers
46	from typing import Iterable
47	
48	from .geometry import Pose3
49	
50	__all__ = ["deskew_point_cloud"]
51	
52	
53	def _real_scalar(value: object, name: str) -> float:
54	    """Coerce one real, finite, non-boolean scalar to float."""
55	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, numbers.Real):
56	        raise TypeError(f"{name} must be a real number, got {type(value).__name__}")
57	    result = float(value)
58	    if not math.isfinite(result):
59	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be finite, got {result!r}")
60	    return result
61	
62	
63	def _point(value: object, name: str) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
64	    """Validate one 3D point of finite, non-boolean real coordinates."""
65	    if isinstance(value, (str, bytes, bytearray)):
66	        raise TypeError(f"{name} must be a sequence of 3 real numbers")
67	    try:
68	        items = tuple(value)  # type: ignore[call-overload]
69	    except TypeError:
70	        raise TypeError(f"{name} must be a sequence of 3 real numbers") from None
71	    if len(items) != 3:
72	        raise TypeError(f"{name} must have 3 coordinates, got {len(items)}")
73	    return (
74	        _real_scalar(items[0], f"{name}[0]"),
75	        _real_scalar(items[1], f"{name}[1]"),
76	        _real_scalar(items[2], f"{name}[2]"),
77	    )

"""Motion compensation (de-skewing) for one timestamped laser scan.

A spinning or scanning LiDAR integrates a frame over time: each beam is
measured at a slightly different instant, so points taken from a moving
platform are skewed in space. :func:`deskew_point_cloud` undoes that skew by
re-expressing every point as if all beams had fired at one reference instant.

The inputs follow the :mod:`mappilot.geometry` convention that a pose maps
local coordinates to parent coordinates
(``p_parent = R * p_local + t``):

* ``trajectory`` samples are ``(time, Pose3)`` pairs; each :class:`Pose3`

def _real_scalar(value: object, name: str) -> float:
    """Coerce one real, finite, non-boolean scalar to float."""
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, numbers.Real):

    """Validate one 3D point of finite, non-boolean real coordinates."""

    e = log( (A X)^{-1} (X B) )

# is at most this threshold are treated as parallel, when deciding whether
# the motion set observably constrains all six extrinsic degrees of freedom.

    input order; ``initial_error`` and ``final_error`` are the weighted
    objectives recomputed from the initial and final poses, so every field
    agrees with the pose it was derived from.

# -- scalar / record validation ------------------------------------------------


def _positive_int(value: object, name: str) -> int:
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, numbers.Integral):
        raise TypeError(f"{name} must be an integer, got {type(value).__name__}")
    result = int(value)
    if result < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a positive integer, got {result}")
    return result


def _positive_float(value: object, name: str) -> float:
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, numbers.Real):
        raise TypeError(f"{name} must be a real number, got {type(value).__name__}")
    result = float(value)
    if not math.isfinite(result):
        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be finite, got {result!r}")
    if result <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be greater than zero, got {result!r}")
    return result


def _weight(value: object, name: str) -> float:
    """Validate one observation weight: a positive, finite, non-boolean real."""
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, numbers.Real):
        raise TypeError(f"{name} must be a real number, got {type(value).__name__}")
    result = float(value)
    if not math.isfinite(result):
        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be finite, got {result!r}")
    if result <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be greater than zero, got {result!r}")
    return result


def _pair(value: object, name: str, length: int) -> tuple:
    """Materialize one fixed-length record; type-error on bad shape."""
    if isinstance(value, (str, bytes, bytearray)):
        raise TypeError(f"{name} must be a sequence of {length} elements")
    try:
        items = tuple(value)  # type: ignore[call-overload]
    except TypeError:

        raise TypeError(f"{name} must have exactly {length} elements, got {len(items)}")

def _unpack_observation(record: object, index: int) -> tuple[Pose3, Pose3, float]:
    """Validate one ``(body_motion, sensor_motion, weight)`` observation."""
    name = f"observations[{index}]"
    items = _pair(record, name, 3)
    body_motion = items[0]
    if not isinstance(body_motion, Pose3):
        raise TypeError(
            f"{name}[0] (body_motion) must be a Pose3, got "
            f"{type(body_motion).__name__}"
        )
    sensor_motion = items[1]
    if not isinstance(sensor_motion, Pose3):
        raise TypeError(
            f"{name}[1] (sensor_motion) must be a Pose3, got "
            f"{type(sensor_motion).__name__}"
